title: incident-bot: add SLO toolkit autodiagnostics helpers and on-call quicklinks
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Add helpers for SLO toolkit autodiagnostics and on-call quicklinks: improves runbook linking relevance and provides sanitized context snippets for responders. Backwards compatible; toggled behind feature flag.
description: Context: on-call engineers need faster access to actionable runbooks and richer diagnostic context during incidents. This PR introduces a set of helper utilities in the SLO toolkit used by incident-bot to (1) prioritize and auto-link runbooks based on SLO and alert context, (2) generate compact, sanitized diagnostic snippets for on-call quicklinks, and (3) provide heuristics to score and surface the most relevant runbooks. Implementation: added internal/slo_toolkit/linker.go with runbook scoring heuristics (weights for SLO overlap, tag matching, recent edits), pkg/diagnostics/helpers.go for sanitized context extraction (prefix trimming, token budget, redaction rules), web/oncall/quicklinks.tsx to surface quicklinks in the UI, configs/runbooks.yaml to tag canonical runbooks, and tests in test/autodiag_helpers_test.go. CI: updated ci/workflows/ci.yml to run the new unit test suite and added a lightweight e2e smoke check for quicklinks. Feature gating: all behavior is behind the feature flag "autodiag_runbook_linking" and will be disabled by default for existing customers. Rollout: staged rollout plan in docs/oncall-runbooks.md; initial internal rollouts to SRE team followed by gradual enablement for paid customers. Motivation: reduces MTTR by surfacing higher-quality runbooks and gives incident-bot the ability to attach focused diagnostic links instead of long lists of unrelated guidance. Backwards compatibility: no breaking API changes; configuration is optional and defaults to current behavior. Testing: unit tests for scoring, redaction, and UI snapshot tests; ran integration smoke tests on staging; manual oncall drill performed by SRE.
